I use iPhone Mirroring on my Mac every day for quick access to my iPhone, and this year the feature is getting even better. Public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate have rolled out this month, bringing three major updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything new.

macOS 27: What's New With iPhone Mirroring

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window using any app that supports iOS 27. Right now, that means only Apple's first-party iPhone apps are supported. However, once developers begin rolling out iOS 27 updates later this year, resize support will expand quickly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only supported three preset sizes: Smaller, Actual Size, and Larger. What's New in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27

expected to launch later this year.

There are a few other updates to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Access Control Center
  • DRM Video Support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring didn't allow access to Control Center. In macOS 27, you can access Control Center with the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or through the "Show" menu in the Mac menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected video on your Mac through iPhone Mirroring. Previously, all DRM-protected videos would simply show a black screen when iPhone Mirroring was enabled.

macOS 27 also introduces a new app icon design for iPhone Mirroring, consistent with the style of several other built-in Apple apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried the public beta? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
